BFIU's ML/TF risk management guidelines for banks add that every employee should complete at least a **day-long basic course with an evaluation**, followed by regular refreshers; that staff should have relevant training **before taking up a desk**; and that the board should have an AML/CFT awareness programme **at least once a year**.

**Recruitment (para 11.1):** screen staff on hiring and post enough skilled officers to the AML division. **Customers (para 11.3):** inform them why information is needed, and use leaflets and posters in every branch.

cards.title: Roles and duties
cards.prompt: Match each role to a duty Circular 26 gives it.

pairs.right: Issues a clear annual statement of commitment to all officers and staff.
Leads the CCC; BFIU must be told at once if the person changes.
Heads the AML & CFT Division; may not be below DGM or senior vice president.
Holds quarterly AML meetings and sends the minutes to the AML division.
Tests branches independently and audits at least 10% more branches each year.
Reports half-yearly to the CEO and board, with a copy to BFIU within two months.

items.label: CCC members
items.detail: Senior heads of departments, led by the CAMLCO; no internal audit staff.

items.label: CCC meetings
items.detail: At least quarterly; more if needed.

items.label: CCC report to BFIU
items.detail: Copy of the half-yearly report (Jan-Jun, Jul-Dec) sent within two months.

items.label: Extra audit coverage
items.detail: Branches tested separately each year beyond the regular audit plan.

items.label: Agents audited yearly
items.detail: Minimum share of agents inspected each year by internal audit.

items.label: Record retention
items.detail: After an account closes (MLPA s.25(1)(b); Circular 26 para 12).

cards.title: The show-cause notice
cards.setting: CAMLCO's office, two months after the inspection.

lines.text: The inspection went well overall, but BFIU has sent a show-cause notice about one branch that missed two STR referrals last year.
Our own audit flagged that branch in March. The fix was agreed but never finished.
Under the MLP Rules, if our reply isn't accepted, BFIU can fine us under section 23 of the MLPA.
And if a fine is imposed, we must also take action against those responsible and tell BFIU within a month. Penalties land on people, not just the bank.
So what do we say in the reply?
The truth, the facts and a credible fix. Let's decide.

cards.title: Answering BFIU
cards.situation: BFIU has issued a show-cause notice to Doyel's CEO: a Rajshahi branch failed to escalate two suspicious cases last year. Internal audit had found the weakness in March, but the agreed fixes (training and a monitoring review) were not completed. The reply is due in ten days.

choices.text: Reply that the cases were minor and the branch staff have since been transferred, so no further action is needed.
choices.outcome: Playing it down does not answer the notice. Under Rule 27 an unacceptable reply lets BFIU impose fines under section 23 of the MLPA, and staff transfers do not fix a control weakness.

choices.text: Reply on time with the facts, an analysis of why the fixes stalled, a dated plan (training, file review, look-back for missed STRs) approved by the CEO and CCC, and the disciplinary steps taken.
choices.outcome: Correct. A frank, timely reply with a credible plan is the best response. If a fine is still imposed, Rule 27(6) requires the bank to take administrative action against those responsible and tell BFIU within one month.

choices.text: Ask for an extension of three months to investigate before replying.
choices.outcome: A short extension can sometimes be reasonable, but asking for months while doing nothing risks the notice being treated as unanswered, which itself allows BFIU to act under Rule 27(2).

choices.text: Blame internal audit for not following up its own finding.
choices.outcome: Audit raised the issue; management and the CCC owned the fix. Shifting blame inside the bank does not help the reply, and BFIU looks at the bank as a whole.

cards.back: Fine of Tk 50,000 to Tk 25 lakh on the bank, plus possible cancellation of the licence of the bank or a branch, booth or agent.
Tk 10,000 a day, up to Tk 5 lakh.
Tk 20,000 to Tk 5 lakh.
Tk 10,000 a day, up to Tk 5 lakh for each instruction not followed.
Owners, directors, officers or contract staff can be fined Tk 10,000 to Tk 5 lakh.
Every owner, director, manager or officer directly involved is deemed guilty unless they prove lack of knowledge or due diligence.

items.label: CEO statement
items.detail: Annual commitment message to all staff.

items.label: Quarterly meetings
items.detail: CCC at least four times a year; branch AML meetings every quarter.

items.label: Half-yearly reviews
items.detail: Branch self-assessments and the CCC report to CEO, board and BFIU.

items.label: Annual audit
items.detail: Independent testing plus at least 10% extra branches.

items.label: Training and refresh
items.detail: Basic, role-based and refresher training; records kept.

cards.question: How long must Doyel keep KYC documents and transaction records for a closed account?
options: One year after the last transaction
At least five years after the account is closed
Three years after the account was opened
Until the customer asks for them to be destroyed
cards.explanation: MLPA section 25(1)(b), Rule 13 of the MLP Rules 2019 and Circular 26 paragraph 12 require at least five years after closure (or after an occasional transaction). Records linked to an investigation are kept until the case is finally settled.

cards.title: Real case: BFIU looks ahead to the APG mutual evaluation
cards.body:
At its May 2026 conference for scheduled bank CEOs and CAMLCOs, BFIU's head told banks to prepare for Bangladesh's **mutual evaluation by the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG) in the 2027-2028 cycle**, stressing institutional readiness. The conference also called for more capacity building, training and modern technology to deal with growing digital risks.

A mutual evaluation tests whether the whole system works in practice, including whether banks really understand their risks, apply CDD, report suspicion and freeze sanctioned funds. Evaluators can visit banks and talk to staff.

What that means for Doyel:

- Training records must show who was trained, on what, and when.
- Self-assessment and audit findings must show closure, not just discovery.
- Front-line staff should be able to explain, in their own words, when and how they escalate a concern.

cards.title: Inspection-ready in five checks
cards.body:
- **Policy:** board approval date, last review, CEO's annual statement circulated.
- **Governance:** CCC membership (7+, no auditors), four meetings, half-yearly reports and BFIU copies.
- **Branches:** BAMLCO nominations stating duties, quarterly minutes, self-assessments.
- **Audit:** independent testing reports, 10% extra branches, follow-up evidence.
- **Records and training:** five-year records, training logs for every officer.

cards.title: Stage five take-aways
items: The board approves the AML/CFT policy; the CEO issues an annual commitment statement to all staff.
The CCC has at least seven senior members, meets at least four times a year, excludes internal auditors and reports half-yearly.
Every branch has a BAMLCO, holds quarterly AML meetings and self-assesses every six months; internal audit tests independently.
All officers need basic, role-based and refresher training; the CAMLCO and DCAMLCO need training or certification; keep the records.
Keep records for at least five years after closure; penalties include fines of up to Tk 25 lakh and licence action, plus fines on staff.

cards.prompt: If an APG evaluator stopped you in a corridor tomorrow and asked what you would do with a suspicious transaction, what would you say, and what record would prove you were trained to do it?

quiz.question: Who must issue an annual statement of commitment to AML/CFT to all of a bank's officers and staff?
options: The head of human resources
The chair of the audit committee
Each branch BAMLCO
The chief executive officer
quiz.explanation: Circular 26 paragraph 1.2(2) requires the CEO to issue a clear and effective statement of commitment every year and direct its implementation.

quiz.question: What is the minimum seniority of a bank's CAMLCO under Circular 26?
options: Exactly one step below the board chair
Any officer, provided BFIU approves the appointment
No more than two steps below the managing director or CEO
Any officer of at least senior principal officer grade
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 1.3(1)(a) says the CAMLCO must not be more than two levels below the MD/CEO; in foreign banks the CAMLCO must be on the top management committee.

quiz.question: How often must the Central Compliance Committee meet?
options: Once a year, before the annual general meeting
Every month, with BFIU present
Only when BFIU announces an inspection
At least four times a year, on a quarterly basis
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 1.3(1)(g) requires the CCC to meet quarterly, at least four times a year, and allows extra meetings as needed.

quiz.question: Who may be nominated as a BAMLCO?
options: The branch manager, the second officer or an experienced senior officer in charge of a key desk
An outside consultant hired by the branch
Any newly recruited officer who has just completed the bank's foundation training, so that the role builds experience
An officer of the internal audit division
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 1.3(4) requires an experienced officer: the branch manager, the second officer, or an experienced senior officer in charge of general banking, foreign exchange, credit or similar.

quiz.question: How often must branches carry out their AML/CFT self-assessment?
options: Every six months, using the checklist in Annex C
Every month, using the CTR template
Only after a BFIU inspection finds a problem
Once every three years, during the external audit
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 8.1(1) requires each branch to assess itself half-yearly against the self-assessment checklist in Annex C.

quiz.question: Besides branches in its regular annual audit plan, what extra coverage must internal audit give to AML/CFT independent testing?
options: One extra branch per division each decade
All branches every month
Separate testing of at least 10% of branches using the Annex D checklist
None; the regular plan is enough
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 8.2(2) requires independent testing during regular audits and a separate programme covering at least 10% of branches, each rated and reported.

quiz.question: What does paragraph 11.2 count as 'suitable training' for bank officers?
options: Basic AML/CFT training plus training on the risks of their work, targeted by level and department, with periodic refreshers
Training only for compliance staff, not for other officers
A single induction video watched once on joining, followed by an annual email reminding staff of the main laws and circulars
An annual email reminding staff of the law
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 11.2(1) and its footnote describe target-oriented training for officers of different levels and departments, covering basics and job-related risks, with refresher training at intervals.

quiz.question: Within what time must a copy of the CCC's half-yearly report reach BFIU?
options: By the end of the following financial year
Within two months after the end of the half-year
Within seven days after the end of the half-year
Only when BFIU asks for it
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 1.3(2) requires the half-yearly report (January-June, July-December), with the CEO's comments, to go to the board and a copy to BFIU within two months of the period's end.

quiz.question: What fine range can BFIU or the regulator impose on a bank that breaches its duties under section 25(1) of the MLPA?
options: Tk 5,000 to Tk 50,000 per breach, with no other consequences for the bank's licence or for its branches and agents
Tk 50,000 to Tk 25 lakh, plus possible licence cancellation for the bank or a branch, booth or agent
A fixed Tk 1 crore for each breach
Twice the bank's annual profit
quiz.explanation: Section 25(2) allows a fine of at least Tk 50,000 and up to Tk 25 lakh, and cancellation of the licence or permission of the organisation or any branch, service centre, booth or agent.

quiz.question: After BFIU fines Doyel for not following an instruction, what must the bank also do under Rule 27(6) of the MLP Rules 2019?
options: Nothing more once the fine is paid, because the fine settles the matter for both the bank and its responsible officers
Take administrative or disciplinary action against the responsible officers and tell BFIU within one month
Publish the fine in two national newspapers
Refund the fine to customers affected
quiz.explanation: Rule 27(6) requires the reporting organisation to take administrative or disciplinary action against the responsible official along with paying the fine, and to inform BFIU within one month.

bank.question: Doyel Commercial Bank's new CAMLCO wants to list the instruments in order of legal force, from highest. Which order is right?
options: The MLP Rules 2019, then the MLPA, then Circular 26, then the ATA
MLPA and ATA, then the MLP Rules 2019, then BFIU Circular 26, then the bank's board-approved policy
BFIU Circular 26, then the MLPA, then the bank's policy, then the MLP Rules 2019
The bank's policy, then the MLP Rules 2019, then the MLPA and ATA, then Circular 26
bank.explanation: The Acts come first; the Government made the MLP Rules 2019 under section 29 of the MLPA; BFIU issues Circular 26 under the Acts; the bank's own policy must fit all of them.

bank.question: A customer is charged with money laundering. His defence says the case must wait until a separate fraud trial ends with a conviction. Which provision answers this?
options: Section 7 of the ATA, which applies the same rule to terrorist financing and requires the predicate trial to finish first
Section 25(2) of the MLPA, which lets BFIU fine the bank instead
Rule 13 of the MLP Rules 2019 on keeping records until a case ends
Section 4(5) of the MLPA: being charged with or convicted of the predicate offence is not a precondition
bank.explanation: Section 4(5) makes clear that a money laundering charge or penalty does not depend on a charge or conviction for the predicate offence. Rule 13 deals with record keeping, not with the elements of the offence.

bank.question: Which statement about BFIU's legal standing is correct?
options: It is a private body funded by banks, with powers given by the Bankers' Association
It is a department of the Ministry of Finance that Bangladesh Bank may consult when it chooses
It is a separate central agency under section 24 of the MLPA with its own office in Bangladesh Bank, and it exercises Bangladesh Bank's powers under the ATA
It is part of the police and needs a court order before contacting any bank
bank.explanation: MLPA section 24 establishes BFIU with its own seal and office inside Bangladesh Bank, and ATA section 15(5) says Bangladesh Bank's ATA powers and duties are exercised by BFIU.

bank.question: Which of these acts falls inside the MLPA's definition of money laundering even if the money was earned lawfully?
options: Moving savings between two of your own accounts at different banks
Paying a supplier in cash for goods actually delivered
Depositing a salary cheque into a joint account with a spouse
Sending money or property abroad irregularly, against the law
bank.explanation: The definition includes sending money or property abroad irregularly, whether it was earned by legal or illegal means. The other actions are ordinary banking activity unless other facts make them suspicious.

bank.question: The board of Doyel Commercial Bank has not approved any instructions on officers' duties for preventing terrorist financing. Who faces personal liability under the ATA?
options: Only the branch BAMLCOs, who face suspension by BFIU
No one personally; only the bank pays a fine of Tk 50,000
The board chair (or the CEO where there is no board), who can be fined up to Tk 25 lakh and removed from office
Only the CAMLCO, who personally faces imprisonment of up to 12 years for every instruction the board fails to issue
bank.explanation: ATA section 16(2) makes the board, or the CEO where there is no board, approve and issue those instructions. Section 16(4) lets Bangladesh Bank fine the chair or CEO up to Tk 25 lakh and remove them from office for failing to do so.

bank.question: Which body gives effect to UN Security Council sanctions in Bangladesh through Statutory Regulatory Orders?
options: The Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission, under its own rules
Each bank's board, by adopting the lists in its own policy
The Anti-Corruption Commission, under the ACC Act 2004
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, under the United Nations (Security Council) Act 1948
bank.explanation: BFIU's guidance on TF and PF explains that MoFA issues SROs under the UN (Security Council) Act 1948. Banks then screen and freeze under the ATA and BFIU's instructions.

bank.question: A cash officer says money laundering is 'only about crime money'. Which part of the MLPA definition shows this is too narrow?
options: It also covers any cash deposit above Tk 10 lakh made in a single day
It also covers every transfer to a foreign account, even a regular one
It also covers late repayment of a bank loan by a business customer, since overdue loans count as proceeds of crime under the Act
It also covers moving lawfully earned money abroad irregularly and structuring transactions to avoid reporting
bank.explanation: Two limbs of the definition do not depend on crime proceeds: irregular transfers abroad (of money earned legally or illegally) and conducting transactions to evade reporting. A large cash deposit is reportable in a CTR but is not itself laundering.

bank.question: What does the jump from 14,106 STRs/SARs in FY 2022-23 to 30,199 in FY 2024-25 mean for a BAMLCO?
options: Each report competes for analysts' attention, so clear grounds for suspicion and full documents matter more than ever
Banks may now file STRs straight from branches without any BAMLCO evaluation, because BFIU wants volume rather than detail
BFIU has stopped disseminating intelligence to investigating agencies
BFIU no longer needs CTRs because STRs cover every cash transaction
bank.explanation: BFIU still disseminates intelligence (199 reports in FY 2024-25). With more reports, well-reasoned STRs with complete documents are what allow BFIU to act. Circular 26 keeps the branch evaluation step.

bank.question: Which pairing of offence and maximum prison term is correct?
options: Terrorist financing under the ATA: up to 20 years' rigorous imprisonment
Terrorist financing under the ATA: up to 12 years' simple imprisonment
Money laundering under the MLPA: up to 7 years or a fine only
Money laundering under the MLPA: up to 20 years' imprisonment
bank.explanation: ATA section 7(3) sets 4 to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment for terrorist financing; MLPA section 4(2) sets 4 to 12 years for money laundering.

bank.question: Doyel's Rajshahi branch opens an account for a company. The directors are named, but 60% of the shares are held by another company registered abroad. What does Circular 26 require?
options: Ask the local directors to sign a declaration that they are the only owners
Accept the foreign company's name as the beneficial owner and file it
Identify the natural persons who ultimately own or control the company and verify their identity from reliable sources
Open the account now and record the foreign shareholder only if it later sends funds into the account or appoints a signatory
bank.explanation: Paragraph 3.4(5) requires the bank to identify the beneficial owner of every account and verify identity to its satisfaction. For companies, that means the people with a controlling ownership interest; if none can be found, a senior managing official. A legal person is not a beneficial owner.

bank.question: Under paragraph 3.4(5), what must the bank do if no natural person can be identified through ownership or control of a corporate customer?
options: Record 'not applicable' and apply simplified due diligence
Identify the relevant person holding a senior management position and record their details
Treat the company secretary as the beneficial owner in all cases
Refuse the account automatically, because ownership is unclear
bank.explanation: Circular 26 and Rule 7(5) of the MLP Rules 2019 say that where no person can be identified through ownership or control, the bank identifies the person in a senior management role.

bank.question: A customer's account was rated low risk at opening. A review now shows frequent large foreign transfers that do not fit her profile. What does Circular 26 expect after the update?
options: Keep the low-risk rating until the next five-year review, because Circular 26 fixes the review cycle and ratings cannot change in between
Close the account because ratings can never be changed
Ask the customer to choose which risk category she prefers
Re-assess the account's risk without delay and move it to high risk if warranted, with the enhanced measures that follow
bank.explanation: Paragraph 3.6(4) requires the risk of an account to be re-assessed promptly after an update and a method for moving accounts from low to high risk. The five-year cycle is a minimum, not a reason to wait.

bank.question: A Dhaka branch offers privilege banking to a high-net-worth customer. What extra requirement applies?
options: Simplified due diligence, because the customer is well known
Only the branch manager's personal approval
Enhanced due diligence in addition to the other CDD instructions
No CDD beyond the standard form, as the customer is wealthy
bank.explanation: Paragraph 3.6(5) requires EDD when a bank provides privilege banking services, on top of its other CDD instructions.

bank.question: A trading company's director lives in a jurisdiction FATF has placed under a call for action. How should Doyel respond?
options: Apply enhanced due diligence to the relationship and its transactions, and any countermeasures FATF calls for
Apply simplified due diligence because the company is registered in Bangladesh
Treat the company as low risk if its trade licence is valid in Bangladesh
Refuse every customer with any link to that country, whatever the facts, and report each refusal to BFIU as a sanctions match
bank.explanation: Paragraph 3.6(6) and Rule 17 require EDD for relationships and transactions with persons or entities from countries that do not meet international standards, such as those on FATF's lists, and FATF countermeasures where applicable.

bank.question: A former influential person left office eight months ago. Her family members now want accounts. According to BFIU's PEP guidance, how should the family members be treated?
options: As ordinary customers subject to normal CDD, unless their own risk calls for more
As customers who cannot be accepted until two years have passed
As high risk for exactly five years after she left office
As PEPs for life, with enhanced due diligence and the CAMLCO's approval required for every account they open
bank.explanation: BFIU's guidance keeps the PEP/IP herself in that category for at least 12 months after leaving office, depending on risk, but says family members should be treated as ordinary customers from the point the PEP/IP leaves office unless risk factors justify EDD.

bank.question: Who must approve opening an account for a foreign PEP under Circular 26?
options: The bank's CAMLCO
BFIU, in writing, before the account is opened
The board of directors in a full meeting
The branch manager alone
bank.explanation: Paragraph 3.10(2) requires the CAMLCO's approval to establish or continue a business relationship with a PEP. BFIU does not pre-approve individual accounts.

bank.question: Doyel plans to launch a new app-based account opening service. When must it assess the ML/TF risk of the service?
options: After the first suspicious transaction is detected on the app
Only if BFIU asks for an assessment during an inspection
Within a year of launch, once enough real transaction data is available to measure the risk the service actually carries
Before the service is launched, with measures in place to manage the risks found
bank.explanation: Paragraph 3.16 requires banks to identify and assess the ML/TF risk of new technology-based products, services or practices, and to put measures in place, before they are introduced.

bank.question: A bank uses agents to serve rural customers. Under Circular 26 paragraph 3.14, who is responsible for the agents' AML/CFT compliance?
options: The bank remains fully responsible, alongside the agent
The local union parishad that certifies the agent
The agent alone, once it signs an agency contract
Bangladesh Bank, because it licenses agent banking
bank.explanation: Paragraph 3.14(1) puts responsibility for compliance with all AML/CFT instructions fully on the bank as well as the agent, and requires agent screening, risk rating, training and monitoring.

bank.question: On 10 March 2026 an officer at Doyel asks whether the bank should still file CTRs weekly, as instructed in January. What is right?
options: No. BFIU cancelled weekly filing by circular letter in February 2026, so monthly CTRs under Circular 26 resumed from March 2026
No. CTRs were abolished in 2024 and replaced by STRs only
Yes. The January 2026 circular letter replaced Circular 26 paragraph 6 permanently, so weekly filing still applies today
Yes, but only for cash deposits; withdrawals are now monthly
bank.explanation: BFIU Circular Letter 1 of 8 January 2026 moved CTRs to weekly filing, but Circular Letter 4 of 26 February 2026 cancelled it and told banks to file under Circular 26 paragraph 6 again from March 2026.

bank.question: In September 2024 an officer argued that cash deposits no longer belonged in CTRs. Was he right then, and is he right now?
options: Right then and right now, because cash deposits were permanently taken out of CTRs in 2024 and never put back
Wrong then and now, because BFIU never changed the CTR rules
Briefly right from August 2024, but BFIU cancelled that change on 24 October 2024, so deposits are included again
Wrong then, but right now, since the 2026 letters removed deposits
bank.explanation: Circular Letter 1 of 15 August 2024 excluded cash deposits from CTRs from August 2024; Circular Letter 2 of 24 October 2024 cancelled that instruction with immediate effect.

bank.question: On one day a customer withdraws Tk 4 lakh at the counter, Tk 3 lakh by ATM and Tk 3.5 lakh at another branch, all from the same account. Is a CTR needed?
options: No. No single withdrawal reached Tk 10 lakh
Only if the customer is already rated high risk
No. ATM withdrawals are never counted
Yes. Cash withdrawals in one account on one day total Tk 10.5 lakh, including ATM cash
bank.explanation: Paragraph 6(1) counts one or more cash deposits or withdrawals in one account on one day, including online and ATM cash. The total here passes Tk 10 lakh.

bank.question: A BAMLCO evaluates a teller's referral and decides it is not suspicious. What should she do with the referral?
options: Destroy the teller's note to protect the customer's privacy, since a referral that is not reported should leave no trace
File an STR anyway, because every referral must be reported
Tell the customer that the matter has been cleared
Record her analysis and observations in writing and keep them, so the decision can be reviewed
bank.explanation: Paragraph 7(3) requires the BAMLCO to analyse referrals and preserve her observations in writing. BFIU's STR guidance stresses documenting decisions not to report as well as decisions to report.

bank.question: Which statement about a CTR and an STR is correct?
options: Filing a CTR satisfies the STR duty for the same transaction
An STR is only needed when the amount is below the CTR threshold, because larger cash amounts are already covered by the CTR
A CTR is a routine threshold report; it never replaces an STR when a transaction is suspicious
CTRs go to Bangladesh Bank, while STRs go to BFIU
bank.explanation: Both go to BFIU on goAML. Paragraph 6(3) says CTR data must be reviewed and anything suspicious filed as an STR; the two duties are separate.

bank.question: During a CDD review, an officer questions a customer so aggressively about an internal investigation that the customer realises he is suspected. How does BFIU's STR guidance view this?
options: It is tipping off only if the officer showed the customer the STR form
It can amount to tipping off, even though the officer never mentioned an STR
It is a customer service issue, not an AML issue
It is acceptable because CDD always takes priority
bank.explanation: BFIU's guidance warns that tipping off can occur when staff approach a client about an internal investigation and intense questioning makes the client aware of it.

bank.question: Which pattern most clearly shows the 'unusual is not yet suspicious' principle in BFIU's STR guidance?
options: A student receives large business payments and the officer closes the alert without questions
A known exporter's receipts jump in the peak season, matching shipping documents, so the officer documents the reason and keeps monitoring
A trader's invoices are far above market prices, and the officer files them without comment
A customer asks how to avoid reports, and the officer explains the CTR threshold
bank.explanation: The guidance says unusual activity is a basis for further enquiry; a convincing explanation backed by documents can resolve it. The other options either ignore red flags or fail to escalate them.

bank.question: What does BFIU Circular Letter 2 of 5 February 2026 ask scheduled banks to do?
options: Stop filing STRs for transactions below Tk 10 lakh
Strengthen their transaction monitoring under Circular 26 paragraph 5 and file STRs without delay where appropriate
Replace manual monitoring with a single software package supplied by BFIU and stop filing STRs until it is installed
File monitoring alerts with BFIU every week instead of STRs
bank.explanation: The circular letter draws attention to paragraph 5 of Circular 26 and instructs banks to strengthen transaction monitoring systems and submit STRs/SARs without delay where applicable.

bank.question: A teller fears being sued by a customer after reporting him in good faith. What should the AML division tell her?
options: Section 28 of the MLPA protects reporting organisations and their staff from legal proceedings for acts done in good faith under the Act
The bank will defend her, but the MLPA offers no protection
She should have asked the customer's consent before reporting
She is protected only if the customer is later convicted; if he is acquitted, she can be sued for defamation
bank.explanation: Section 28 bars civil, criminal, administrative or other proceedings against reporting organisations, their boards and staff for acts done in good faith under the MLPA or its rules.

bank.question: A screening hit on a remittance beneficiary shares a name with a UN-listed person, but the nationality and date of birth differ and the customer has a verified NID. What is the best course?
options: Freeze the funds permanently and report a sanctions match to BFIU, because any shared first and last name counts as a true match
Report it to BFIU as a sanctions match by the next working day
Ask the beneficiary whether he is the person on the UN list
Clear it as a false positive after checking the identifiers, record the reasons with approval, and release the remittance
bank.explanation: Paragraph 10(4) and BFIU's guidance expect banks to resolve hits using identifiers and keep false positive records. Asking the customer is pointless and could alarm him.

bank.question: A news report links a Doyel account holder to proliferation financing, but the person is on no list. Which Circular 26 duty still applies?
options: None, because only listed persons are covered
Ask Bangladesh Bank's foreign exchange department for advice first
Send detailed information about the account to BFIU without delay
File the account in the next monthly CTR
bank.explanation: Paragraph 10(2) requires a bank to send BFIU details without delay whenever the media reports TF or PF links to someone holding an account, whatever the list status.

bank.question: A bank's screening tool screens account titles but not beneficial owners or controllers. Why is this a gap under Circular 26?
options: It is not a gap, because beneficial owners need screening only once, at account opening, and never again after that
It is a gap only for accounts opened before 2020
Paragraph 10(4) covers accounts held directly or indirectly by listed persons, by those they control and by associates
Screening rules apply only to wire transfers, not to accounts
bank.explanation: Paragraph 10(4) requires checks for accounts or transactions in the name of listed persons, or directly or indirectly controlled by them, or of their associates. BFIU's guidance stresses beneficial ownership in sanctions compliance.

bank.question: An entity is convicted of terrorist financing. Besides action under section 18, what fine does section 7(4) of the ATA allow?
options: Up to Tk 5 lakh, as an administrative penalty
Three times the value of the property involved or Tk 50 lakh, whichever is higher
A fixed Tk 25 lakh, payable to BFIU
Twice the value or Tk 10 lakh, whichever is higher
bank.explanation: Section 7(4)(a) allows a fine of three times the value or Tk 50 lakh, whichever is higher, and section 7(4)(b) exposes the entity's head to 4 to 20 years. Twice the value or Tk 10 lakh applies to individuals.

bank.question: A bank fails to freeze the funds of a UN-listed entity promptly as section 20A requires. What penalty range applies?
options: Imprisonment of the CAMLCO for up to 12 years
A fine of Tk 5 lakh to Tk 25 lakh or twice the suspected funds, whichever is higher, and possible licence suspension
A fine of Tk 10,000 a day up to Tk 5 lakh, with no effect on the licence of the bank or its branches, booths or agents
A warning letter for the first breach only
bank.explanation: ATA section 20A(5) sets the fine for failing to follow BFIU's instructions or to freeze without delay, and allows Bangladesh Bank to suspend the licence of the agency or its branches, booths or agents.

bank.question: Why should Doyel's sanctions list include entities proscribed by the Government of Bangladesh as well as UN lists?
options: Domestic lists apply only to NGOs, not to banks
Only UN lists are legally binding on banks; domestic lists are shared for information and need no action unless BFIU asks
Circular 26 requires screening against both UN lists and persons or entities listed or proscribed by the Government
BFIU screens domestic lists centrally, so banks need not
bank.explanation: Paragraphs 2(2), 10(3) and 10(4) cover both UN-listed persons and those listed or proscribed by the Government. The 2023 proscription letter showed BFIU expects banks to act on domestic proscriptions at once.

bank.question: Which proliferation-related UN regimes does BFIU's TF/PF guidance list for a bank's compliance programme?
options: No UN regimes; only domestic lists apply to proliferation
Resolutions 1540, 1718, and 1737 with its successors including 2231
Resolutions 1267 and 1373 only
Resolutions 1988 and 2253 only
bank.explanation: The guidance lists 1267 and 1373 (terrorism) and 1540, 1718 and 1737/2231 (proliferation) as regimes against which reporting organisations should build compliance.

bank.question: Before a bank pays out a domestic wire transfer, which information should travel with it under paragraph 9.1(2)?
options: Originator information as for cross-border wires, unless the payment is to a Government or autonomous body or is inter-bank
The originator's information only if the amount exceeds Tk 10 lakh
Only the amount and date of the transfer
Nothing, because domestic wires never carry ML/TF risk and Circular 26 limits wire transfer rules to cross-border payments
bank.explanation: Paragraph 9.1(2) applies the paragraph 9.1(1) requirements to domestic wires. Wires to Government, semi-government or autonomous bodies and inter-bank dealings are not covered.

bank.question: A foreign bank's Dhaka operation names a CAMLCO who is three levels below the country CEO and not on the management committee. What does Circular 26 require?
options: In a foreign bank the CAMLCO must be a member of the top management committee
Only BFIU's written approval of the appointment
That the CAMLCO be based in the bank's home country
Nothing; foreign banks are outside Circular 26
bank.explanation: Paragraph 1.3(1)(a) sets the two-levels rule and adds that, for foreign banks, the CAMLCO must be a member of the top management committee. BFIU must be told at once if the CAMLCO changes.

bank.question: Doyel's management wants to give the CAMLCO responsibility for retail sales as well. What must it first be sure of?
options: That BFIU has approved the CAMLCO's new salary
That the board chair agrees to act as deputy CAMLCO
That the CAMLCO has passed a sales qualification
That the extra duty will not disrupt the bank's AML/CFT work
bank.explanation: Paragraph 1.3(1)(a) requires management to make sure, before giving the CAMLCO any other duty, that the bank's AML/CFT activities will not be hampered.

bank.question: Internal audit finds a serious risk issue in a branch's self-assessment report. What does paragraph 8.2(1) require?
options: Report the branch directly to the police
Wait for the next annual audit cycle
Visit the branch immediately and inform the AML division
Ask the branch to re-submit the report in six months
bank.explanation: Paragraph 8.2(1) requires internal audit to inspect a branch at once when a risky issue appears in its self-assessment and to inform the AML division.

bank.question: Which list of topics must a BAMLCO's quarterly branch AML meeting cover under paragraph 1.3(5)?
options: Customer complaints and branch renovation plans
Only cases that BFIU has already asked about
KYC, transaction monitoring, identifying and reporting suspicious activity, sanctions lists and UN resolutions, self-assessment, record keeping and training
Deposit targets, loan recovery, staff leave rosters and branch renovation plans, with AML issues taken only when BFIU raises them
bank.explanation: Paragraph 1.3(5) lists customer identification, transaction monitoring, suspicious transaction identification and reporting, implementation of UN resolutions including the local sanctions list, self-assessment, record keeping and training. Minutes go to the AML division.

bank.question: Rezaul's audit finds 40% of officers at a branch have had no formal AML training. Which combination of rules makes this a finding?
options: Circular 26 para 11.2 requires suitable training for all officers, and BFIU's guidelines expect a basic course with evaluation before staff take up a desk
Only the bank's HR manual, because BFIU sets training rules for the CAMLCO and DCAMLCO but none for other officers or new staff
Training is optional unless the branch handles foreign exchange
The MLPA requires training only for the CAMLCO, so there is no finding
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11.2 requires suitable training for all officers with refreshers, and BFIU's ML/TF risk management guidelines call for a basic course with evaluation and training before placement. Rule 6(3) of the MLP Rules 2019 also makes officer training part of the compliance programme.

bank.question: Which records does paragraph 12 add beyond customer and transaction files?
options: Personal social media accounts of BAMLCOs
Copies of customers' tax returns for ten years
Staff salary records and branch utility bills
Records of AML/CFT training, meetings, audits, inspections and special inspections
bank.explanation: Paragraph 12(2) requires banks to keep information and documents on AML/CFT training, meetings, audits/inspections and special inspections, alongside the five-year customer records in paragraph 12(1).

bank.question: Records relating to an account under investigation would normally reach their five-year limit next month. What does Rule 13 of the MLP Rules 2019 say?
options: Destroy them on schedule to protect customer privacy
Keep them until the related case is finally disposed of
Send the originals to the customer before destroying copies
Keep them for exactly six more months
bank.explanation: Rule 13(d) requires records connected with an inquiry or investigation to be kept until the case is finally settled, beyond the general five-year period.

bank.question: BFIU fines Doyel for failing to supply information on time. Which individuals can also be fined under section 23(8) of the MLPA?
options: Only the customers whose accounts were involved, since bank staff cannot be fined personally under the MLPA for late information
Owners, directors, officers, employees or contract staff responsible, Tk 10,000 to Tk 5 lakh each
Only BFIU officers who requested the information
No individual can be fined under the MLPA
bank.explanation: Section 23(8) lets BFIU fine responsible owners, directors, officers, staff or contractual personnel between Tk 10,000 and Tk 5 lakh when the organisation is fined under section 23(3)-(6).

bank.question: A bank is fined by BFIU more than three times in one financial year under section 23(3)-(5). What can follow under Rule 27(3)?
options: Nothing more, because fines are the only sanction BFIU may use; licence action belongs to Bangladesh Bank alone and needs a court order
BFIU can suspend the licence of the bank or a branch, service centre, booth or agent, and inform the licensing authority
Transfer of the bank's ownership to BFIU
Automatic criminal conviction of the board
bank.explanation: Rule 27(3) describes suspension of a licence when an organisation faces more than three fines in a financial year, with business stopped until BFIU lifts it; the licensing authority must report its action to BFIU within a month.

bank.question: The CCC and internal audit both want to own branch AML testing. How does Circular 26 divide their roles?
options: The CCC and AML division run the programme and evaluate results; internal audit tests independently and sends its reports to the AML division
Both merge into one committee chaired by the head of audit
BFIU assigns the role case by case after each inspection
Internal audit runs the AML programme and evaluates results, while the CCC audits internal audit's work and reports to BFIU each quarter
bank.explanation: Paragraphs 1.3 and 8 keep them separate: no auditor sits on the CCC, internal audit carries out independent testing and sends rated reports to the AML division, which prepares the evaluation report for management.
